The Clear Cup That Still Needed a Test

看起来清澈却仍需检验的那杯水 · 639 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A school laboratory compared two filters for a model drinking-water system. In the first experiment, a blue dye went into a transparent container. Water from one filter looked clear. Water from the other still had a faint stain. A student named Mei began to write that the first device made the water safe. Her chemistry teacher asked her to stop. A liquid could lose its color without losing a harmful substance. The class would have to define exactly what the experiment could show.

2The pupils examined the layers. Powder could bind dye to its surface. They called this absorption at first, then corrected the term to adsorption. A second layer held microscopic particles suspended in the fluid. It could not remove every soluble compound. Mei recorded the mass and concentration of identical samples before either went through. They chose a transparent container so a change in the intensity of the color could be compared without moving the sample.

3The control stood between both filters. Its color became lighter without any treatment. A microscope showed a fine solid. The formulation contained an artificial preservative, and another powder did not dissolve completely. The teacher asked whether a chemical reaction could change the appearance without making anything safer. The teacher rejected the theory that a color change necessarily meant purification. Some particles had settled. That distinction made the control more useful than a quick claim about a clear cup.

4Mei repeated the test with a measured amount of soluble dye. She used a thermometer to keep both samples at the same temperature. A loose lid had allowed vapor to escape and condense on one jar. Condensation on its cooler wall showed how much water had moved. Differences in humidity could also change how fast water left an open container. Mei closed both lids and drew a line at the initial level. The teacher noted that a fair comparison required consistency in details as well as identical materials.

5The teacher introduced a neutral sample and asked the class to predict its reaction. A chart distinguished hydrogen from oxygen and showed how atoms interacted in a compound. A highly concentrated dye could bind differently from a weak one. Its characteristic color made change easy to detect. A sensitive instrument could detect smaller variations. It could not tell them whether mold had begun to grow in the surroundings. They planned a test before interpreting any biochemical change. If the process was reversible, they could learn something about the transformation of the dye.

6A biology class examined a sealed specimen under supervision. Ordinary microscopy could detect tissue or a worm. It could not establish the absence of bacteria or predict the progression of later growth. Odor might indicate decay. An odorous sample was no conclusive proof of a specific poison. The pupils made a rational classification of what they observed and sent the remaining fluid to a qualified laboratory for biological analysis.

7The report measured a reduction in one chemical, not all contamination. A biochemist explained why a protein test, a measure of oxygen, and a genetic test answered different questions. A diagram showed a gene inside a cell nucleus. Organisms could be genetically distinct even when they looked alike. A change in appearance could reflect an adaptive response or a developmental stage. Mei added the distinction rather than generalize from a single stain.

8A visitor asked to drink from the clear cup. Mei put it by the other sample. A label explained how boiling affected one hazard and another discussed chemical purity. The teacher asked whether a biological variant, a physical filter, and an atomic measurement answered the same question. The visitor could infer a color change from what he saw. He could not infer a change in an organism's reproductive function. Mei pointed to the intermediate stage at which the next test would begin.

四级汇总词汇 · 18中文译文

看起来清澈却仍需检验的那杯水

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1学校实验室给饮用水模型比较两种过滤器。第一次实验，把蓝色染料倒进透明容器。一个过滤器出来的水看着清澈，另一个还带一点颜色。学生小梅准备写，第一台机器让水变安全了。化学老师叫她先停一停。水褪色时，有害成分仍可能留在里面。他们要先说清，这个实验究竟能证明什么。

2学生看过滤器的各层。细粉能把染料留在表面。他们起初叫它“吸收”，后来改成“吸附”。第二层能拦下一些悬浮在液体里的细小颗粒，但无法去掉所有可溶性化合物。过滤前，小梅给两份完全相同的样品记下质量和浓度。透明容器让他们不用搬动样品就能比较颜色深浅。

3对照样放在两种过滤器之间。没处理过，颜色也变浅了。显微镜下能看见细小固体。配方含人工防腐剂，另有一种粉末没全溶开。老师问，化学反应会不会只改变外观。她否定了“变色必然意味着净化”的说法。有些颗粒只是沉到了底部。有了这个区别，对照样比一杯看起来清澈的水更能说明问题。

4小梅重新取定量可溶染料做试验。她用温度计确认两份样品同温。一个罐盖松了，水汽逸出，在罐壁凝结。冷壁上的水滴显示有多少水从原处跑掉。湿度不同，敞口容器失水速度也会不同。她盖紧两个盖子，在起始水位画线。公正的比较既要用一样的材料，也要注意细节一致。

5老师拿来一份中性样品，请全班预测反应。示意图把氢和氧区分开，画出原子在化合物里怎样相互作用。浓染料的吸附可能和稀的不同。特有颜色便于观察，灵敏仪器还能测出细微变化，但看不出周围是否开始长霉。大家先设计检验，再解读生化变化。如果过程可以逆转，他们就能多了解一点染料怎样变了。

6生物课在监督下检查密封样品。普通显微观察能看见组织或小虫，不能证明没有细菌，也不能预测之后会怎么繁殖。异味可能意味着腐败，单凭气味不能认定是哪种毒物。学生按看见的现象作了合理分类，再把剩下的液体送到合格实验室作生物分析。

7报告量出某种化学物质减少了多少，并未检验所有污染。一名生化人员解释，蛋白质检测、含氧量测量和基因检测回答的是不同的问题。图上显示基因在细胞核里。两种生物看着相似，基因却可能不同。外观改变还可能来自环境适应或生长阶段。小梅把这一区别补进展板，没有从一抹颜色推及所有样品。

8观众问能不能喝那杯清水。小梅把杯子放回另一份样品旁。一个标签说明煮沸能影响哪种风险，另一个讲化学纯度。老师请观众想一想，生物差异、物理过滤和原子尺度的检测，是否在回答同一个问题。从眼前的杯子能推断颜色变了，不能推断生物的繁殖功能变了。小梅指向实验流程的中间环节，下一个检验就从这里开始。
